name: Radio channels
description: Music as a channel: songs from your Jellyfin library, or an internet radio station, shown with the cover, the lyrics and a visualizer that moves with the sound, in one of five looks. A 24/7 music channel, or music between shows. Needs Chrome or Edge on this computer.
author: SchedularrTV
lowPowerNotice: each station on air is a hidden browser drawing its page without a graphics chip, plus a live encode. Prefer a plain colour background over the blurred cover, Bars or Waveform over Spectrum, and a look other than Vinyl, and capture at about 10 frames per second.

settings.label: Browser
settings.description: Chrome, Edge or Chromium, run hidden to draw the stations. Leave empty to find one automatically.
settings.lowPowerNote: On Raspberry Pi OS, install chromium (sudo apt install chromium); Chrome and Edge have no ARM Linux builds.

settings.label: ffmpeg
settings.description: Leave empty to use the ffmpeg set under App settings.

settings.label: Stream address
settings.description: How ErsatzTV reaches this scheduler. Leave empty unless ErsatzTV runs on another machine or in a container.

settings.label: Capture frames per second
settings.description: How often the page is captured (5 to 30). The visualizer is drawn from the sound at the stream's own frame rate (App settings → Hardware and video encoding).
settings.lowPowerNote: About 10 here (the default): lyrics and the clock don't need more.

settings.label: Keep a station running after it goes off air (seconds)
settings.description: So back-to-back radio segments don't restart the station each time.

settings.label: Draw animations at the capture rate
settings.description: The hidden browser moves the page's animations (the spinning record, the scrolling ticker, the glow) on only as often as it's captured, instead of redrawing 60 times a second for frames that are never used. They move at the same speed. Turn off only if an animation stops or stutters.
